admission.justification: The near-linear bound on fully paired inputs constrains every future change to the gap pass: a slower pairing regresses the sealed scaling witnesses.

alternatives.option: A live Fenwick count/rank/removal index over number order per side, with identical strict-between bounds and pair-one-each-side rule
alternatives.reason: O(N log N) cardinality work with pairing outcomes identical by construction on every input.

R3 measurement of the R2 replacement implementation (per-gap full side slices over sorted intervals with hash-membership checks): N^2/4+N-1 membership calls on crossed fully-paired reordered inputs at 500-4000 references. A different implementation and metric from the R1 linear-value-scan cubic implementation in context; both rejected in favor of the chosen live Fenwick index.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A future pairing rule needs order information the number-order index cannot carry.

consequences: Fully paired monotone and crossed populations show identical operation counts with exact injective maps; pairing policy, order and witnesses are unchanged.
context: Cost history of the singleton-gap pass across three retained code attempts.
